units.title: Why Types
units.tip: TypeScript adds type annotations to JavaScript, allowing you to specify what type each variable must be. The TypeScript compiler checks your code before it runs, catching errors early. JavaScript runs the compiled result, which is pure JavaScript with no types.

exercises.question: What does TypeScript add to JavaScript?
exercises.answer: Type annotations and a compile-time type checker
exercises.explain: TypeScript lets you declare what type each variable is. The compiler checks these types before your code runs, finding bugs early.
choices: Type annotations and a compile-time type checker

exercises.question: What does it mean to compile TypeScript?
exercises.answer: Transform TypeScript into plain JavaScript that runs in browsers or Node
exercises.explain: The TypeScript compiler converts your .ts files to .js files. The JavaScript is what actually runs. All type information is removed.
choices: Transform TypeScript into plain JavaScript that runs in browsers or Node

exercises.question: What is the benefit of type checking?
exercises.answer: Catch errors at compile time instead of at runtime
exercises.explain: With types, the compiler catches mistakes like passing the wrong type to a function. Without types, the error happens when the code runs.
choices: Catch errors at compile time instead of at runtime

exercises.question: What is type inference?
exercises.answer: The compiler automatically figures out a type from the value
exercises.explain: If you write let x = 5, TypeScript infers x is a number without you writing : number explicitly.
choices: Checking if a type is correct
The compiler automatically figures out a type from the value

exercises.question: Can compiled TypeScript code run without TypeScript?
exercises.answer: Yes, TypeScript compiles to plain JavaScript which runs anywhere
exercises.explain: The output is just JavaScript. A browser or Node.js does not know or care that the original was TypeScript.
choices: Yes, TypeScript compiles to plain JavaScript which runs anywhere
Only if you keep the .ts files nearby
No, the environment must support TypeScript

exercises.question: Why is TypeScript useful in large projects?
exercises.answer: Types make code clearer and prevent many bugs before runtime
exercises.explain: In large codebases, types document what functions expect and return. They also catch refactoring mistakes automatically.
choices: It eliminates the need for testing
Types make code clearer and prevent many bugs before runtime

exercises.question: What is a tsconfig.json file?
exercises.answer: Configuration file that controls how TypeScript compiles
exercises.explain: tsconfig.json specifies compiler options like the target JavaScript version, where to output files, and which files to include.
choices: Configuration file that controls how TypeScript compiles

exercises.question: Do TypeScript types exist when the program runs?
exercises.answer: No, types are erased when the code is compiled to JavaScript
exercises.explain: Types only exist while the compiler checks your code. The JavaScript it produces has no type annotations, so types cannot be inspected at run time.
choices: Yes, every value carries its TypeScript type
No, types are erased when the code is compiled to JavaScript
Only when running in a browser

exercises.question: What does it mean when you type a function parameter?
exercises.answer: You specify what type of value the parameter must be
exercises.explain: function greet(name: string) means the name parameter must be a string. Calling greet(123) is a type error.
choices: You specify what type of value the parameter must be

exercises.question: How does TypeScript help during refactoring?
exercises.answer: The compiler catches places where renamed or changed functions are called incorrectly
exercises.explain: If you rename a function or change its parameters, TypeScript shows all the places that break immediately during compilation.
choices: The compiler catches places where renamed or changed functions are called incorrectly

units.title: Basic Types
units.tip: TypeScript includes primitive types like string, number, and boolean. Arrays can hold specific types. Tuples group values of different types. Any and unknown are escape hatches. Void means no return value.

exercises.question: What is the string type?
exercises.answer: A sequence of characters, text data
exercises.explain: string is the type for text. You can write let name: string = 'Alice' or let message: string = "hello".
choices: A sequence of characters, text data

exercises.question: What is the number type?
exercises.answer: Integers, decimals, and special values like Infinity and NaN
exercises.explain: number covers all numeric values: 5, 3.14, -10, Infinity, and NaN.
choices: Integers, decimals, and special values like Infinity and NaN

exercises.question: What is the boolean type?
exercises.answer: True or false values
exercises.explain: boolean holds exactly two values: true and false. Used in conditions and logic.

exercises.question: What is the any type?
exercises.answer: An escape hatch that disables type checking for that variable
exercises.explain: any means the variable can hold any type. It bypasses type safety. Avoid it if possible.
choices: An escape hatch that disables type checking for that variable
A type that holds all types

exercises.question: When should you use any?
exercises.answer: Only when you really cannot determine the type, as a last resort
exercises.explain: Using any defeats the purpose of TypeScript. Use unknown instead if you need flexibility while keeping some safety.
choices: Only when you really cannot determine the type, as a last resort

exercises.question: How do you type an array of numbers?
exercises.answer: number[] or Array<number>
exercises.explain: Both number[] and Array<number> mean an array containing only numbers. You can use either syntax.

exercises.question: What is a tuple?
exercises.answer: An array with a fixed length and specified types at each position
exercises.explain: A tuple like [string, number] is an array with exactly 2 elements: a string and a number in that order.
choices: An array of fixed size but any types
An array with a fixed length and specified types at each position

exercises.question: What is the unknown type?
exercises.answer: Like any, but safer: you must check the type before using the value
exercises.explain: unknown is type-safe. You cannot use it without first narrowing it to a specific type with a typeof check.
choices: Like any, but safer: you must check the type before using the value

exercises.question: What is the void type?
exercises.answer: Used for functions that do not return a value
exercises.explain: A function returning void does not return anything. For example, function log(msg: string): void { console.log(msg); }
choices: Used for functions that do not return a value

exercises.question: What is the null type?
exercises.answer: A type representing the absence of any value
exercises.explain: null is a specific value meaning nothing, and it is different from undefined. With strict null checks on, a variable can only be null if its type says so.
choices: A type representing the absence of any value

units.title: Functions and Objects
units.tip: Function types specify parameter and return types. Optional parameters use ?. Objects type the shape of data, with property types. Readonly prevents modification. Union types allow multiple possibilities.

exercises.question: How do you type a function parameter?
exercises.answer: Use a colon and the type after the parameter name
exercises.explain: function add(a: number, b: number) means both a and b must be numbers.
choices: Use a colon and the type after the parameter name
Write the type before the function name

exercises.question: How do you specify a function return type?
exercises.answer: Use : type after the parameter list, before the opening brace
exercises.explain: function add(a: number, b: number): number { return a + b; } returns a number.
choices: Use : type after the parameter list, before the opening brace
Write return: type in the function body

exercises.question: What is an optional parameter?
exercises.answer: A parameter with ? that does not have to be provided when the function is called
exercises.explain: function greet(name?: string) means name can be omitted. It will be undefined if not provided.
choices: A parameter with ? that does not have to be provided when the function is called
A parameter with a default value
A parameter at the end of the list
A parameter that can be any type

exercises.question: How do you provide a default value for a parameter?
exercises.answer: Use = value after the type
exercises.explain: function greet(name: string = 'Alice') means if name is not provided, it defaults to 'Alice'.

exercises.question: What is an arrow function?
exercises.answer: A concise function syntax using => instead of the function keyword
exercises.explain: const add = (a: number, b: number): number => a + b is an arrow function. It is equivalent to function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
choices: A concise function syntax using => instead of the function keyword
A function that returns an arrow

exercises.question: How do you type an object with properties?
exercises.answer: Use { propertyName: type } syntax
exercises.explain: const person: { name: string; age: number } = { name: 'Alice', age: 30 } specifies object shape.

exercises.question: What does the readonly keyword do?
exercises.answer: Prevents a property from being modified after assignment
exercises.explain: const person: { readonly name: string } means person.name cannot be changed after the object is created.
choices: Prevents a property from being modified after assignment

exercises.question: What is a union type?
exercises.answer: A type that can be one of several specified types
exercises.explain: string | number means the value can be either a string or a number, but not both.
choices: An object type with multiple properties
A type that can be one of several specified types

exercises.question: What is an optional property?
exercises.answer: A property with ? that does not have to be present
exercises.explain: { name: string; age?: number } means age can be missing. If missing, it is undefined.
choices: A property with a default value
A property that can be any type
A property with ? that does not have to be present

exercises.question: Can you add properties to an object that are not in its type?
exercises.answer: No, TypeScript will report a type error
exercises.explain: If you type an object with { name: string }, you cannot add a new property like age without a type error.
choices: No, TypeScript will report a type error

units.title: Interfaces and Type Aliases
units.tip: Interfaces define object shapes and can extend other interfaces. Type aliases define any type, not just objects. Union and intersection types combine types. Literal types specify exact values.

exercises.question: What is an interface?
exercises.answer: A named object type that defines the shape of an object
exercises.explain: interface Person { name: string; age: number; } defines a shape. You can then type variables as Person.
choices: A named object type that defines the shape of an object

exercises.question: What is a type alias?
exercises.answer: A name for any type, created with the type keyword
exercises.explain: type Name = string | null defines a type alias. Type aliases are more flexible than interfaces.
choices: A name for any type, created with the type keyword

exercises.question: What does extends do in interfaces?
exercises.answer: Creates a new interface that inherits properties from another
exercises.explain: interface Student extends Person { grade: number; } has all properties of Person plus grade.
choices: Creates a new interface that inherits properties from another

exercises.question: What is an intersection type?
exercises.answer: A type that combines properties of multiple types
exercises.explain: type Combined = A & B combines types A and B. The result must have all properties from both.
choices: A type that is either of two types
A type that combines properties of multiple types

exercises.question: Can you use type aliases for objects and union types?
exercises.answer: Yes, type aliases can define any type
exercises.explain: type can be used for objects, unions, primitives, tuples, and more. interface is limited to objects.
choices: Yes, type aliases can define any type

exercises.question: What is a literal type?
exercises.answer: A type that represents one exact value
exercises.explain: type Direction = 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right' allows only those exact strings, not any string.
choices: A type for string literals only
A type that is always literal
A type that represents one exact value

exercises.question: What are literal types useful for?
exercises.answer: Restricting a variable to specific allowed values
exercises.explain: Using literal types catches mistakes where an invalid value is used, like 'invalid' when only 'up', 'down', 'left', 'right' are allowed.
choices: Restricting a variable to specific allowed values

exercises.question: Can interfaces and types be used interchangeably?
exercises.answer: Mostly yes for object types, but types are more flexible
exercises.explain: Both can define object shapes, but type supports unions, tuples, and primitives. For objects, prefer interface for consistency.
choices: Mostly yes for object types, but types are more flexible

exercises.question: What is a discriminated union?
exercises.answer: A union type where each member has a shared property to distinguish them
exercises.explain: type Response = { status: 'success'; data: string } | { status: 'error'; error: string }. The status property tells them apart.
choices: A type that includes all fields from all options
A union type where each member has a shared property to distinguish them

exercises.question: When is an interface declaration merged with another?
exercises.answer: When two interface declarations have the same name
exercises.explain: TypeScript merges interface Person { name: string; } and interface Person { age: number; } into one with both properties.
choices: When two interface declarations have the same name
When they have the same properties

units.title: Narrowing and Generics
units.tip: Narrowing refines a variable's type with checks. typeof checks the type at runtime. Generic functions accept any type while staying type-safe. Constraints limit what generics can be.

exercises.question: What is type narrowing?
exercises.answer: Refining a variable to a more specific type within a code block
exercises.explain: After if (x !== null), TypeScript knows x is not null in the following block, narrowing its type.
choices: Refining a variable to a more specific type within a code block

exercises.question: What does a typeof check do?
exercises.answer: Checks the type of a value at runtime
exercises.explain: if (typeof x === 'string') narrows x to string in that block. Useful for union types.
choices: Checks the type of a value at runtime

exercises.question: What is a type guard?
exercises.answer: A runtime check that narrows a variable to a specific type
exercises.explain: typeof, instanceof, property checks, and custom predicates are type guards. They help TypeScript narrow types safely.
choices: A runtime check that narrows a variable to a specific type
A function that returns a type

exercises.question: How do you check if a value is null or undefined?
exercises.answer: Using x !== null && x !== undefined or x ?? operations
exercises.explain: Checking !== null or using the nullish coalescing operator ?? narrows out null and undefined.
choices: Using x !== null && x !== undefined or x ?? operations

exercises.question: What is instanceof?
exercises.answer: A check to see if an object is an instance of a class
exercises.explain: if (err instanceof Error) checks if err is an Error instance. Useful for narrowing to specific classes.
choices: A check to see if an object is an instance of a class

exercises.question: What is a generic type parameter?
exercises.answer: A placeholder for a type that is specified when the function is used
exercises.explain: function identity<T>(x: T): T returns the same type T that was passed in. T is a type parameter.
choices: A type that works with anything
A placeholder for a type that is specified when the function is used
A type that is generic to all functions

exercises.question: Why use generics?
exercises.answer: To write reusable functions that work with any type while preserving type safety
exercises.explain: Without generics, you would use any and lose type safety. Generics let a function work with multiple types safely.
choices: To write reusable functions that work with any type while preserving type safety

exercises.question: What is a generic constraint?
exercises.answer: A condition that restricts what types a generic can accept
exercises.explain: function getLength<T extends { length: number }>(x: T) requires T to have a length property.
choices: A condition that restricts what types a generic can accept
A requirement for the function body

exercises.question: How do you specify a generic for an array?
exercises.answer: Array<T> or T[] where T is the element type
exercises.explain: Array<string> and string[] both mean an array of strings. Use whichever you prefer.
choices: Array<T> or T[] where T is the element type

exercises.question: Can a function have multiple generic type parameters?
exercises.answer: Yes, using comma-separated names like <T, U>
exercises.explain: function pair<T, U>(a: T, b: U): [T, U] has two type parameters T and U.
choices: No, only one generic per function
Yes, using comma-separated names like <T, U>

units.title: Classes and Modules
units.tip: Classes group properties and methods. Access modifiers (public, private, protected) control visibility. Implements uses an interface as a contract. Import and export make code modular. Enums define named constants.

exercises.question: What is a class?
exercises.answer: A blueprint for creating objects with properties and methods
exercises.explain: class Person { name: string; constructor(name: string) { this.name = name; } } defines a Person class.
choices: A blueprint for creating objects with properties and methods

exercises.question: What does public access modifier mean?
exercises.answer: The property or method is accessible from outside the class
exercises.explain: public (or no modifier, which is default) means anyone can access it. const p = new Person('Alice'); console.log(p.name) works.
choices: The property is part of the interface
The property or method is accessible from outside the class
The property is in the constructor

exercises.question: What does private access modifier mean?
exercises.answer: The property or method can only be accessed from inside the class
exercises.explain: private secret: string can only be read or written within the class, not from outside.
choices: The property is hidden from the interface
The property or method can only be accessed from inside the class

exercises.question: What does protected access modifier mean?
exercises.answer: The property is accessible inside the class and in subclasses
exercises.explain: protected name can be accessed in the class and in any class that extends it, but not from outside.
choices: The property is accessible inside the class and in subclasses

exercises.question: What is a constructor?
exercises.answer: A special method that runs when an object is created
exercises.explain: constructor(name: string) { this.name = name; } is called when you write new Person('Alice').
choices: A special method that runs when an object is created
A method that builds the class

exercises.question: What does implements do?
exercises.answer: Makes a class promise to follow an interface contract
exercises.explain: class Dog implements Animal ensures Dog has all properties and methods required by the Animal interface.
choices: Copies an interface into a class
Makes a class promise to follow an interface contract

exercises.question: What does export do?
exercises.answer: Makes a value, class, or function available to other files
exercises.explain: export const PI = 3.14 or export class Person { } lets other files import and use them.
choices: Makes a value, class, or function available to other files

exercises.question: What does import do?
exercises.answer: Brings a value, class, or function from another file into the current file
exercises.explain: import { PI } from './constants' or import Person from './Person' makes exported items available locally.
choices: Brings a value, class, or function from another file into the current file

exercises.question: What is an enum?
exercises.answer: A named set of constants representing related values
exercises.explain: enum Direction { Up, Down, Left, Right } lets you use Direction.Up instead of magic strings or numbers.
choices: A named set of constants representing related values

exercises.question: Why use enums instead of string literals?
exercises.answer: Enums provide named constants, preventing typos and making code clearer
exercises.explain: Direction.Up is clearer and safer than 'up'. Misspelling Direction.Upp is caught by the compiler.
choices: Enums provide named constants, preventing typos and making code clearer
